nodes.description: Distortion product otoacoustic emission testing was abnormal in every affected member of the family, which places the lesion in the cochlea rather than in the middle ear or in the retrocochlear auditory pathway. Bone conduction thresholds and oto-immittance measurements were obtained in order to exclude a conductive component. No cell type, molecular function or biological process is bound to this node, because the source establishes cochlear dysfunction and no more: no temporal bone, imaging or electrophysiological study beyond DPOAE has been published for this family.

nodes.description: The loss begins at the high frequencies and extends to involve all frequencies as it progresses. Audiogram configurations across the family were sloping, flat or residual. The authors note that this pattern is shared with several other ADNSHL loci and with presbycusis, which is part of why the entity is hard to recognise outside a large pedigree.

nodes.description: Bilateral, sensorineural and postlingual in every affected member. Onset was in the second decade of life in most cases; the earliest clinical evidence in the family was at age 14, in two individuals. Severity ranged from mild to profound and varied within as well as between generations, and there was no apparent effect of sex on progression. Sixteen of the 48 genotyped family members were classified as affected for linkage. HPO annotates OMIM:609965 with sensorineural hearing impairment at 16/16 and juvenile onset, both from this one report.

nodes.description: Linkage and recombinant haplotype analysis place the disease allele between D14S581 and D14S1021, a 9.6 cM interval at 14q11.2-q12 containing about 6.4 Mb and roughly 60 known genes. The statistical evidence for the interval is strong - a maximum multipoint LOD score of 5.4 - but the gene, the variant and the gene product are all unknown, so nothing downstream of this node can be stated at the molecular level. The node is marked PROVISIONAL for that reason: the locus is established, the mechanism is not.
